verses.gurmukhi: ਹਉਮੈ ਅਭਿਮਾਨ ਕੈ ਅਗਿਆਨਤਾ ਅਵਗਿਆ ਗੁਰ ਨਿੰਦਾ ਗੁਰ ਦਾਸਨ ਕੈ ਨਾਮ ਗੁਰਦਾਸ ਹੈ ॥
verses.translit_en: haumai abhimaan kai agiaanataa avagiaa gur ni(n)dhaa gur dhaasan kai naam gurdhaas hai ||

en.bdb: Under the influence of self-pride, ego and ignorance, I show scant respect to the Guru and indulge in slander of his servants. Yet I have named myself the slave of Guru.

verses.gurmukhi: ਮਹੁਰਾ ਕਹਾਵੈ ਮੀਠਾ ਗਈ ਸੋ ਕਹਾਵੈ ਆਈ ਰੂਠੀ ਕਉ ਕਹਿਤ ਤੂਠੀ ਹੋਤ ਉਪਹਾਸ ਹੈ ॥
verses.translit_en: mahuraa kahaavai meeThaa giee so kahaavai aaiee rooThee kau kahit tooThee hot upahaas hai ||

en.bdb: This is like poisonous root or tuber of Aconytum Ferox (Mitha Mauhra) that is called sweet or an infected eye that is called 'akh ai hai' and one who suffers from smallpox is said to have been visited and blessed by mother (Mata). This is a big joke.

verses.gurmukhi: ਬਾਂਝ ਕਹਾਵੈ ਸਪੂਤੀ ਦੁਹਾਗਨਿ ਸੁਹਾਗਨਿ  ਕੁਰੀਤਿ ਸੁਰੀਤਿ ਕਾਟਿਓ ਨਕਟਾ ਕੋ ਨਾਸ ਹੈ ॥
verses.translit_en: baa(n)jh kahaavai sapootee dhuhaagan suhaagan  kureet sureet kaaTio nakaTaa ko naas hai ||

en.bdb: Just out of fun a barren woman is called Saputi (one blessed with sons), an abandoned woman is called happily married, it is no different than calling an evil rite as auspicious or one with chopped nose as beautiful.

verses.gurmukhi: ਬਾਵਰੋ ਕਹਾਵੈ ਭੋਰੋ ਆਂਧਰੈ ਕਹੈ ਸੁਜਾਖੋ ਚੰਦਨ ਸਮੀਪ ਜੈਸੇ ਬਾਂਸੁ ਨ ਸੁਬਾਸ ਹੈ ॥੧੯੧॥
verses.translit_en: baavaro kahaavai bhoro aa(n)dharai kahai sujaakho cha(n)dhan sameep jaise baa(n)s na subaas hai ||191||

en.bdb: Just as a crazy person is called simple, a blind person called sighted. Similarly a bamboo tree even in close proximity to a Sandalwood tree cannot acquire its fragrance, so would I, named Gurdas, cannot qualify to be the slave of Guru. (191)
